subject: math
title: Multiplying by One-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 4 Multiplying by One-Digit Numbers Worksheets: × 10, 100, 1000, Area Models, Partial Products (Free, Ontario)
standard_text: Represent and solve problems involving the multiplication of two- or three-digit whole numbers by one-digit whole numbers and by 10, 100, and 1000, using appropriate tools, including arrays
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on multiplying by one-digit numbers for the Ontario curriculum: multiplying by 10, 100 and 1000, area models, partial products, 3-digit × 1-digit, estimating first and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Split the number into hundreds, tens and ones. Multiply each part, then add the parts.
key_sub: 23 × 4 = 20 × 4 + 3 × 4 = 80 + 12 = 92. To multiply by 10, 100 or 1000, the digits move 1, 2 or 3 places to the left: 40 × 10 = 400. Estimate first to check your answer.
body_html:
Multiply by 10, 100 and 1000

When you multiply by 10, every digit moves one place to the left. A zero fills the empty ones place. × 100 moves the digits two places, and × 1000 moves them three places.

MultiplyThinkAnswer
36 × 1036 tens360
36 × 10036 hundreds3600
4 × 10004 thousands4000
40 × 1040 tens400 (not 4000)

Two digits: split into tens and ones

23 × 4 means 4 groups of 23. Each 23 is 2 tens and 3 ones. Multiply the tens, multiply the ones, then add.

An area model shows the same thing. The rectangle is 23 long and 4 wide. Split 23 into 20 and 3.

Three digits: partial products and the standard method

Partial products write each part on its own row, then add the rows. The standard method is a short way to write the same steps. Start with the ones. If you get 10 or more, write the ones digit and regroup: write a small digit above the next place. Multiply first, then add the regrouped digit.

Estimate first

Round the big number, then multiply. The estimate tells you about how big the answer should be.

Estimate, then check

389 × 6 = ?

389 rounds to 400. 400 × 6 = 2400. Now multiply: 9 × 6 = 54, write 4, regroup 5. 8 × 6 = 48, plus 5 = 53, write 3, regroup 5. 3 × 6 = 18, plus 5 = 23. 2334 is close to 2400, so it makes sense.

Answer: 2334

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting to regroup (23 × 4 = 82)12 ones = 1 ten and 2 ones. Add the 1 ten to the tens: 92
Multiplying only the ones (23 × 4 = 32)Multiply the tens too: 20 × 4 = 80, 3 × 4 = 12, 80 + 12 = 92
Adding an extra zero (40 × 10 = 4000)40 is 4 tens. 40 tens = 400. × 10 adds only one zero
Writing 20 × 4 as 820 × 4 = 2 tens × 4 = 8 tens = 80
Adding the regrouped digit first ((3 + 2) × 4)Multiply first: 3 × 4 = 12, then add 2: 14

faq.q: What multiplication do Grade 4 students learn in Ontario?
faq.a: The Ontario math curriculum asks Grade 4 students to multiply two- and three-digit numbers by one-digit numbers, and by 10, 100 and 1000, using tools such as arrays, base ten blocks and area models. They also use mental math to multiply by 10, 100 and 1000.
Partial products split a number by place value and multiply each part. For 23 × 4, multiply 20 × 4 = 80 and 3 × 4 = 12, then add: 80 + 12 = 92.

faq.q: How do you multiply by 10, 100 and 1000 in your head?
faq.a: Each digit moves one, two or three places to the left, and zeros fill the empty places. So 36 × 10 = 360, 36 × 100 = 3600 and 4 × 1000 = 4000, while 40 × 10 is 400, not 4000.

faq.q: Why should students estimate before they multiply?
faq.a: An estimate shows about how big the answer should be. For 389 × 6, 400 × 6 = 2400, so 2334 makes sense, but an answer like 258 or 23 340 shows a mistake.

items.e: 6 × 1000 = 6 thousands = 6000. Each digit moves three places to the left, so write three zeros after 6.

sets.title: Word problems: hockey, field trips and more

items.q: Olivia buys 3 hockey sticks at $45 each. She pays with $200. How much change does she get?
Hockey cards come in packs of 10. Leah has 46 packs. How many cards does she have?
items.e: Multiply: 46 × 10. 46 × 10 = 46 tens = 460. Each digit moves one place to the left, so write one zero after 46. So the answer is 460 cards.

items.q: For the Terry Fox Run, each of 8 classes at a school in Ottawa raises $126. How much do they raise in all?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: $126 × 8. Ones: 6 × 8 = 48. Write 8, regroup 4 tens. Tens: 2 × 8 = 16, plus 4 = 20. Write 0, regroup 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 1 × 8 = 8, plus 2 = 10. Write 10. Answer: 1008. So the answer is $1008.

items.q: A summer camp buys 7 tents. Each tent costs $289. About how much do the tents cost?
items.e: Round $289 to the nearest hundred: $300. $300 × 7 = $2100. (The exact cost is 289 × 7 = $2023, close to $2100.)

items.q: A school has 6 boxes of pencils with 125 pencils in each box. It gives out 480 pencils. How many pencils are left?
A Grade 4 class reads for 35 minutes every school day. How many minutes is that in 5 school days?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 35 minutes × 5. Ones: 5 × 5 = 25. Write 5, regroup 2 tens. Tens: 3 × 5 = 15, plus 2 = 17. Write 17. Answer: 175. So the answer is 175 minutes.

items.q: A school library has 7 shelves of chapter books. Each shelf holds 145 books. How many books is that?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 145 books × 7. Ones: 5 × 7 = 35. Write 5, regroup 3 tens. Tens: 4 × 7 = 28, plus 3 = 31. Write 1, regroup 3 hundreds. Hundreds: 1 × 7 = 7, plus 3 = 10. Write 10. Answer: 1015. So the answer is 1015 books.

items.q: On a canoe trip in Algonquin Park, a group paddles 18 km each day for 6 days. How far do they paddle?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 18 km × 6. Ones: 8 × 6 = 48. Write 8, regroup 4 tens. Tens: 1 × 6 = 6, plus 4 = 10. Write 10. Answer: 108. So the answer is 108 km.

items.q: An orchard fills 9 crates with apples. Each crate holds 124 apples. How many apples is that?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 124 apples × 9. Ones: 4 × 9 = 36. Write 6, regroup 3 tens. Tens: 2 × 9 = 18, plus 3 = 21. Write 1, regroup 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 1 × 9 = 9, plus 2 = 11. Write 11. Answer: 1116. So the answer is 1116 apples.

items.q: A skating rink keeps rental skates on racks. Each rack holds 36 pairs. There are 7 racks. How many pairs of skates is that?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 36 pairs × 7. Ones: 6 × 7 = 42. Write 2, regroup 4 tens. Tens: 3 × 7 = 21, plus 4 = 25. Write 25. Answer: 252. So the answer is 252 pairs.

items.q: A school books 4 small buses for a field trip. Each bus has 48 seats. 175 people go on the trip. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Step 1: seats: 4 × 48 = 192 (8 × 4 = 32, write 2, regroup 3; 4 × 4 = 16, plus 3 = 19). Step 2: empty seats: 192 − 175 = 17. (Regroup a ten to subtract the ones: 12 − 5 = 7.)

items.q: A sugar bush sells maple taffy in boxes of 10 pieces. It sells 80 boxes on a Saturday in March. How many pieces of taffy is that?
items.e: Multiply: 80 × 10. 80 × 10 = 80 tens = 800. Each digit moves one place to the left, so write one zero after 80. The zero already in 80 stays. Do not add extra zeros: the answer is 800, not 8000. So the answer is 800 pieces.

items.q: An arena in Hamilton has 6 sections. Each section has 238 seats. How many seats are there?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 238 seats × 6. Ones: 8 × 6 = 48. Write 8, regroup 4 tens. Tens: 3 × 6 = 18, plus 4 = 22. Write 2, regroup 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 2 × 6 = 12, plus 2 = 14. Write 14. Answer: 1428. So the answer is 1428 seats.

items.q: A school has 6 Grade 4 classes. Each class has 28 students. About how many Grade 4 students are there?
items.e: Round 28 to the nearest ten: 30. 30 × 6 = 180. (The exact answer is 28 × 6 = 168, close to 180.)

items.q: 3 flocks of Canada geese land on a pond. Each flock has 47 geese. How many geese land on the pond?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 47 geese × 3. Ones: 7 × 3 = 21. Write 1, regroup 2 tens. Tens: 4 × 3 = 12, plus 2 = 14. Write 14. Answer: 141. So the answer is 141 geese.

items.q: Tickets to a hockey game cost $28 each. Noah buys 4 tickets for his family. How much does he pay?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: $28 × 4. Ones: 8 × 4 = 32. Write 2, regroup 3 tens. Tens: 2 × 4 = 8, plus 3 = 11. Write 11. Answer: 112. So the answer is $112.

items.q: A truck driver drives 386 km each day. How far does he drive in 5 days?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 386 km × 5. Ones: 6 × 5 = 30. Write 0, regroup 3 tens. Tens: 8 × 5 = 40, plus 3 = 43. Write 3, regroup 4 hundreds. Hundreds: 3 × 5 = 15, plus 4 = 19. Write 19. Answer: 1930. So the answer is 1930 km.

items.q: A box holds 100 craft sticks. The art teacher orders 25 boxes. How many craft sticks is that?
items.e: Multiply: 25 × 100. 25 × 100 = 25 hundreds = 2500. Each digit moves two places to the left, so write two zeros after 25. So the answer is 2500 craft sticks.

items.q: A roll of raffle tickets has 1000 tickets. The school uses 4 rolls at its winter carnival. How many tickets is that?
items.e: Multiply: 4 × 1000. 4 × 1000 = 4 thousands = 4000. Each digit moves three places to the left, so write three zeros after 4. So the answer is 4000 tickets.

items.q: A store sells winter boots for $129 a pair. It sells 7 pairs on a snowy Saturday. How much money is that?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: $129 × 7. Ones: 9 × 7 = 63. Write 3, regroup 6 tens. Tens: 2 × 7 = 14, plus 6 = 20. Write 0, regroup 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 1 × 7 = 7, plus 2 = 9. Write 9. Answer: 903. So the answer is $903.
